text: A small company manufactures customized bicycles. Whenever the sales department receives an order, a new process instance is created. A member of the sales department can then reject or accept the order for a customized bike. In the former case, the process instance is finished. In the latter case, the storehouse and the engineering department are informed. The storehouse immediately processes the part list of the order and checks the required quantity of each part. If the part is available in-house, it is reserved. If it is not available, it is back-ordered. This procedure is repeated for each item on the part list. In the meantime, the engineering department prepares everything for the assembling of the ordered bicycle. If the storehouse has successfully reserved or back-ordered every item of the part list and the preparation activity has finished, the engineering department assembles the bicycle. Afterwards, the sales department ships the bicycle to the customer and finishes the process instance.

verdict.justification: No gap found, but 3 requirement(s) from the text could not be associated with any clear activity in the observed process -- neither confirmed nor refuted. This verdict is NOT a confirmation of full faithfulness.
verdict.scope: This verdict covers the causal reachability of the requirements expressed in the source text, not the general quality of the process model -- a multiplicity defect (an activity executed more than once due to a mismatched branching structure) is not covered by this verdict, even if the process is otherwise well-formed.

The source text states: “Whenever the sales department receives an order, a new process instance is created.”  
Because no activity in the observed process can be linked to the sales department receiving an order, we cannot confirm or deny whether this requirement is satisfied. The condition cannot be verified with the available information. (This same root cause also affects: Inform storehouse and engineering department, Ship bicycle to customer, engineering department prepared, order accepted, order rejected, part list processed, sale department accepts, sale department rejects, storehouse back ordered, storehouse informed, storehouse processed, storehouse reserved.)

non_verifiable.explanation: The source text says: “Afterwards, the sales department ships the bicycle to the customer and finishes the process instance.” This statement shows that something must be true before the activity “process instance finished” can happen, but the text does not tell us what that something is. Because the condition is not linked to any observable activity in the process, we cannot check whether it is met or not. Therefore, we cannot confirm or refute conformance for this requirement.
